chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Thabit ibn Shuraih, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man marries a woman and then divorces her before entering into her, there is no waiting period (iddah) upon her, and she may marry whenever she wishes from that moment, and it is considered one single divorce.

key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: Waiting period (iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman divorced before consummation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that a pre-consummation divorce (Talaq al-Kunuth) does not require the woman to observe an Iddah, allowing her to remarry immediately, as the divorce is counted as one of the three permissible talaqs. This ruling is derived from the principle that the marital bond is not fully solidified without consummation, distinguishing it from post-consummation divorces. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the financial and temporal obligations of the husband in such cases.
